newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Grajewo wood firm to invest PLN 110 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Grajewo wood firm to invest PLN 110 mln.

text.p: Wood-panel producer ZPW Grajewo SA, participating in Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) scheme, will invest 110 million zlotys to raise production, a spokeswoman for the fund controlling it said on Wednesday.
Marta Fita of Fund No. 15 told Reuters that the financing would be provided by three Polish banks -- Powszechny Bank Kredytowy, Bank Handlowy and Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy.
"The installation of a second production line in Grajewo, which will be possible thanks to the loan, will let the firm double its production in two years," she said.
Agreement on the syndicated loan, signed on Tuesday, will pave the way for the biggest single injection of capital to a company belonging the NFI programme.
Under the scheme, control over more than 500 companies was given to 15 funds, which aim to increase the value of their firms through restructuring, modernisation and privatisation.
NFI No. 15 wants to place Grajewo on the Warsaw bourse later this year.
Poland's 28 million adults are entitled to buy the so-called mass privatisation units in the NFI funds, which will later be exchanged into shares and traded on the bourse.
Grajewo, employing 990 people, netted 12.4 million zlotys on turnover of 195.7 million zlotys in 1995.
